scope: REQ-linked differential slices for accepted http-core-v1 hardening and protocol boundaries; not full OSS nginx behavioral parity
outOfScope: Complete nginx OSS request/response differential suite

slices.notes: Canonical URI vs raw request_uri comparison matrix recorded in the REQ
Nginx accepts deep pipelines; SDKWork http1MaxPipelineDepth is intentional hardening
Pinned probe records nginx idle frames without proactive PING
Early upstream response + request lifecycle differential
keepalive_time vs SDKWork proactive connectionMaximumAge retirement

Single-page full-surface behavioral regression (REQ-2026-0040): routing, URI semantics, static, proxying, LB, filters, limits, TLS SNI, http2 ALPN, stream; the probe owns mock upstreams, staging render, and server lifecycle (see the REQ for the alignment findings it closed). `cases` is the executed-case floor: tools/run-nginx-behavioral-corpus.mjs fails the gate when the probe reports fewer cases than declared, so deleting a case cannot silently shrink coverage.

Conditional requests, byte ranges and cache policy compared field by field against a real nginx binary (REQ-2026-0071). Uniquely, this slice owns its oracle: tests/nginx/differential/nginx-oracle.json is the real-nginx side, so the comparison still runs where nginx is absent. `cases` is the executed-case floor enforced by tools/run-nginx-differential.mjs.

Broad HTTP surface compared field by field against a real nginx 1.29.6 binary (static delivery/MIME/HEAD/ranges incl multipart/conditionals, routing and rewrite, response headers, error_page mapping, gzip negotiation, allow/deny + auth_basic, limit_req/limit_conn, proxy_pass URI splice/Host-forwarded/hop-by-hop/upstream status mapping). Wave 4a added the nginx referer module ($invalid_referer), geo and split_clients variable blocks. Wave 3b added the HTTP/2 `http2_max_concurrent_streams` ingress mapping (proven over real TLS/ALPN h2 connections) and `proxy_method`. Wave 3a/3a-2 added the nginx autoindex family (html/json/jsonp/xml listings), empty_gif and the loopback-gated stub_status page, plus Wave 3a's charset family and gzip refinements. Wave 3a added the nginx charset family (charset/charset_types/source_charset/override_charset header filter) and the gzip refinements (gzip_disable msie6/regex user-agent gating, gzip_proxied Via policy). The slice owns its oracle: tests/nginx/differential-http/nginx-oracle.json is the real-nginx side, so the comparison still runs where nginx is absent; intentional differences are justified per-field in compare.py. Wave 10 added the bounded rewrite/variable engine cases: server/location `set` expansion feeding a request-time `proxy_pass`, `if` truthiness and regex conditions with conditional literal `add_header` (matching and non-matching), location-regex capture `$1` in a variable `proxy_pass`, and request-time `alias $variable` confined by the operator documentRootAllowlist. `cases` is the executed-case floor enforced by tools/run-nginx-differential-http.mjs, and the oracle is pinned to nginx/1.29.6 by the same gate.

PRD-nginx-compatibility §5/§6 virtual-host selection and bounded named-location internal redirects compared against a real nginx 1.29.6 binary: exact / leading wildcard (any depth, longest) / trailing wildcard (longest) / dot-prefix / regex (authored order, nginx case folding) precedence, default-server fallback, and try_files/error_page → @named targets (return, root, proxy_pass). The slice owns its oracle: tests/nginx/differential-host/nginx-oracle.json is the real-nginx side, so the comparison still runs where nginx is absent; intentional differences (nginx's built-in 404 page body) are justified in compare.py. `cases` is the executed-case floor enforced by tools/run-nginx-differential-host.mjs.

Wave 5 CGI-family + memcached slice, extended by Wave 6 gRPC: deterministic FastCGI/uWSGI/SCGI responders echo PARAMS/STDIN; compares parameter mapping (http-level fastcgi_param/uwsgi_param/scgi_param inheritance, automatic HTTP_* fields, HTTP_HOST rule, fastcgi_split_path_info/SCRIPT_NAME/PATH_INFO, fastcgi_index, uwsgi modifier1/modifier2/uwsgi_string), request-body framing, fastcgi_hide_header/fastcgi_pass_header variants, fastcgi_intercept_errors + error_page, and fastcgi_next_upstream failover against real nginx 1.29.6. Bounded nginx `set $memcached_key` support feeds memcached_pass: hit/HEAD/large-value byte-identical, miss 404, raw ERROR 502 and intercepted 502->error_page; generated nginx error-page bodies are status-only allowances for miss/raw-error/405. The Wave 6 gRPC cases (Rust HTTP/2 mock responder, plaintext h2c and verified TLS) compare: unary body+trailers byte-identical, trailers-only non-zero grpc-status rendering, body+trailing grpc-status/message, 3-message server streaming, grpc_set_header overrides plus client-header passthrough (mock echoes :path/:authority/:scheme), grpc_hide_header/grpc_pass_header, missing trailers, grpc_read_timeout 504, grpcs positive with a trusted CA and negative with an unrelated CA, grpc_next_upstream failover, unreachable upstream 502 and grpc_intercept_errors on an upstream HTTP error status; generated-error 504/502 bodies are status-only allowances. Wave 7A transport: `*_bind` source-address binding (mock echoes the accepted peer), `fastcgi_keep_conn` reuse proven by the mock connection id (the pool returns a connection only after a clean END_REQUEST), and typed-plane `unix:` FastCGI/uWSGI targets confined by `[http] unixSocketRoot` (the oracle uses nginx `*_pass unix:` while the gateway side runs a typed JSON configuration in a separate process, since the nginx compatibility plane intentionally fails closed on unix targets). `cases` is the executed-case floor.

Wave 4b stream slice: one connection battery drives the rendered fixture against real nginx 1.29.6 and the runtime, recording byte-level per-connection outcomes. Cases: the bounded stream variable engine (`set` literal value, `map` over an accept-time fact, and `map $ssl_preread_server_name` from a synthetic TLS ClientHello) feeding `return <value>`; pass-through proxying behind the ordered stream access phase (allow/deny, including a deny that closes silently without proxying), stream `return <value>` literal response, stream `limit_conn` (over-limit connection closed silently, slot released after the holder disconnects) and `limit_conn_dry_run` (over-limit connections counted but still proxied). FIN-vs-RST races on a server-closed connection are normalized to one `closed` outcome in battery.py; everything else is compared exactly. The slice owns its oracle (nginx-oracle.json) and its orchestrator; `cases` is the executed-case floor enforced by tools/run-nginx-differential-stream.mjs.
